original_value: Location-based services (LBS) form the main part of the Internet of Things (IoT) and have received a significant amount of attention from the research community as well as application users due to the popularity of wireless devices and the daily growth in users. However, there are several risks associated with the use of LBS-enabled applications, as users are forced to send their queries based on their real-time and actual location. Attacks could be applied by the LBS server itself or by its maintainer, which consequently may lead to more serious issues such as the theft of sensitive and personal information about LBS users. Due to this fact, complete privacy protection (location and query privacy protection) is a critical problem. Collaborative (cache-based) approaches are used to prevent the LBS application users from connecting to the LBS server (malicious parties). However, no robust trust approaches have been provided to design a trusted third party (TTP), which prevents LBS users from acting as an attacker. This paper proposed a symbiotic relationship-based leader approach to guarantee complete privacy protection for users of LBS-enabled applications. Specifically, it introduced the mutual benefit underlying the symbiotic relationship, dummies, and caching concepts to avoid dealing with untrusted LBS servers and achieve complete privacy protection. In addition, the paper proposed a new privacy metric to predict the closeness of the attacker to the moment of her actual attack launch. Compared to three well-known approaches, namely enhanced dummy location selection (enhanced-DLS), hiding in a mobile crowd, and caching-aware dummy selection algorithm (enhanced-CaDSA), our experimental results showed better performance in terms of communication cost, resistance against inferences attacks, and cache hit ratio.

result.paraphrase: Location-based services (LBS) are a major component of the Internet of Things (IoT) and have attracted substantial interest from both researchers and application users because wireless devices are increasingly popular and user numbers keep growing. Yet LBS-enabled applications involve several risks, since users must submit queries based on their true, real-time location. Attacks may come from the LBS server itself or from its operator, potentially causing more serious problems such as the loss of sensitive, personal information about LBS users. For this reason, full privacy protection covering both location and query privacy is a critical issue. Collaborative cache-based methods are employed to stop LBS application users from connecting directly to malicious LBS servers. However, no strong trust mechanisms have been proposed for building a trusted third party (TTP) that prevents LBS users from becoming attackers. This paper proposes a symbiotic relationship-based leader approach to ensure complete privacy protection for users of LBS-enabled applications. In particular, it introduces the mutual-benefit idea behind symbiosis, along with dummies and caching, to avoid interacting with untrusted LBS servers and to achieve full privacy protection. The paper also presents a new privacy metric for estimating how close an attacker is to the time of her actual attack launch. Experimental results against three established methods—enhanced dummy location selection (enhanced-DLS), hiding in a mobile crowd, and caching-aware dummy selection algorithm (enhanced-CaDSA)—showed superior performance in communication cost, resistance to inference attacks, and cache hit ratio.
